- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth with 5-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted average (positive sentiment = 1.1x, negative = 0.9x).  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment momentum (last 3 sentiment values) to adjust forecast direction.
